questions.q: Which of these is NOT an energy store?
questions.explain: Current is a rate of flow of charge, not an energy store. The stores are kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, chemical, magnetic, electrostatic and nuclear.

questions.q: A ball is thrown straight up. As it rises (before reaching the top), which energy transfer mainly occurs?
questions.explain: As the ball rises it slows down, so its kinetic store falls while its gravitational potential store rises: energy is transferred from kinetic to gravitational potential.

questions.q: A stretched elastic band stores energy in which store?
questions.explain: Stretching or compressing a spring or band stores energy in the elastic potential store.

questions.q: A 1500 kg car travels at 20 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy.
A 2.0 kg book is lifted onto a shelf 1.8 m high. Take g = 9.8 N/kg. Calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy.
A spring of spring constant 200 N/m is extended by 0.10 m. Calculate the elastic potential energy stored (limit of proportionality not exceeded).
A 0.50 kg ball moves at 6.0 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy.
How much energy is needed to raise the temperature of 2.0 kg of water by 30 degrees C? Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/kg degC.
questions.explain: Delta E = m c Delta theta = 2.0 x 4200 x 30 = 252 000 J.

questions.q: A 0.50 kg aluminium block gains 9000 J of energy and rises by 20 degrees C. Calculate the specific heat capacity of aluminium.
questions.explain: Rearranging Delta E = m c Delta theta gives c = Delta E / (m Delta theta) = 9000 / (0.50 x 20) = 9000 / 10 = 900 J/kg degC.

questions.q: In the specific heat capacity required practical, why is a layer of insulation wrapped around the metal block?
options: To reduce energy lost to the surroundings
questions.explain: Insulation reduces energy dissipated to the surroundings, so more of the electrical energy supplied raises the block's temperature, giving a more accurate value of c.

questions.q: A motor transfers 6000 J of energy in 30 s. Calculate its power.
A 2000 W kettle is switched on for 90 s. Calculate the energy transferred.
questions.explain: Rearranging P = E / t gives E = P t = 2000 x 90 = 180 000 J.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between energy and power?
options: Power is energy stored; energy is the rate of transfer
Energy is measured in watts; power in joules
Power is the rate at which energy is transferred
Energy and power are the same quantity
questions.explain: Power is the energy transferred per second (P = E/t), measured in watts; energy is measured in joules. Confusing the two is a common error.

questions.q: A child slides down a slide and ends up moving more slowly than a frictionless calculation predicts. Where has the 'missing' energy gone?
options: Dissipated as thermal energy by friction
questions.explain: Energy is conserved and cannot be destroyed. Friction dissipates energy to the thermal store of the slide and surroundings, so less reaches the kinetic store.

questions.q: Which method would best reduce unwanted energy transfers between a machine's moving parts?
questions.explain: Lubrication reduces friction between moving parts, reducing energy dissipated to the thermal store. Insulation and streamlining are other valid methods of reducing unwanted transfers.

questions.q: A house is insulated with material of low thermal conductivity. What is the main effect?
options: Energy is transferred through the walls faster
Energy is transferred through the walls more slowly
The house gains energy from outside
questions.explain: Lower thermal conductivity reduces the rate at which energy is transferred through the walls, so the building cools down more slowly.

questions.q: A motor is supplied with 500 J and usefully transfers 350 J to the kinetic store. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.
questions.explain: Efficiency = (useful output / total input) x 100 = (350 / 500) x 100 = 70%.

questions.q: A lamp is 20% efficient and usefully transfers 4 J as light. Calculate the total energy supplied to it.
questions.explain: Efficiency = useful / total, so total = useful / efficiency = 4 / 0.20 = 20 J.

questions.q: Why can the efficiency of a real device never be 100%?
options: Some energy is always dissipated to less useful stores
Power and energy are different quantities
questions.explain: Energy is conserved, but some is always dissipated (e.g. as thermal energy through friction or heating), so useful output is always less than total input.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy resource?
questions.explain: Wind is renewable as it is replenished and will not run out. Coal, natural gas and nuclear fuel are finite (non-renewable) resources.

questions.q: Which energy resource is most reliable for continuous large-scale electricity generation?
questions.explain: Fossil-fuel power stations can run on demand at any time, making them reliable, whereas solar, wind and wave depend on the weather and time of day.

questions.q: What is a major environmental drawback of burning fossil fuels for electricity?
options: They release carbon dioxide, contributing to climate change
They use up the world's water
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide (a greenhouse gas) plus other pollutants, contributing to global warming and acid rain. Radioactive waste is a drawback of nuclear power, not fossil fuels.
